terms.gloss: go to the dogs, go to ruin
evidence: Plaut. Cist. 2.1.12; Tac. A. 1.79 (Lewis & Short s.v. pessum)
terms.comment: Pessum, “to the bottom”, lives on in a few phrases, mostly early and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short). To ruin something is pessum dare.
Traupman’s phrase, “the affair has tilted”; not found as a phrase in Lewis & Short or the Latinitas loci collections, so Traupman is the only evidence.

phrases.english: that the most fertile plains of Italy would go to ruin

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 97, checked against the searchable text and the page images of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
